Working with film-crew (single-shot mode), then banana-pro-director-2.0 (Mode 3B, pure environment plate).

**Session start:** this folder isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check for open items. I didn't change any files, so there's no notes entry or push.

**Assumptions** (non-interactive run, so I decided these myself)
- **Engine:** Banana Pro on Higgsfield, the skill's default. 16:9, 2K. You set the aspect ratio in the UI, not in the prompt.
- **No references attached.** The text describes the whole room.
- **Late-November highlands:** a light early snow on the far ridges and none on the pit floor.
- **Generic location:** no real company, logo or readable text. A real mine or brand needs your approval first.
- **Built for compositing:** the camera is locked off at seated-adult eye height. Everything is in focus front to back, which keeps the window view sharp. The chairs leave clear spaces where people can be placed later. The light is flat overcast daylight from the window only, so the plates you add will match.

**Crew plan (short)**
- **Director:** the room is quiet before a hard meeting. The pit outside the window is the reason the room exists, so it is the focal point at the far end.
- **Production design:** a sober renovated office. Pale-grey walls, one wall of honey-colored local volcanic stone, a long walnut-veneer table and grey mesh chairs. Small details hint at the work: a tray of drill-core samples with green copper staining, white hard hats, a rolled pit plan, a water carafe. One personal touch: a finished small cup of coffee with grounds left in it.
- **DP:** about a 28mm-equivalent lens, eye level, one-point perspective down the table to a full-width window. The window is the only light source. The sky is the brightest value and keeps its cloud detail. The darkest value is under the table, where some detail stays visible. Soft contact shadows. Fine-grain daylight film look, muted natural grade.

## FINAL

**Mode 3B: pure environment plate, Banana Pro (Higgsfield), 16:9, 2K, no references**

```
A cinematic still photograph of an empty company meeting room on a real location, captured locked-off on a tripod at seated-adult eye height from the near end of a long conference table, a calm one-point composition looking straight down the length of the table toward a full-width window that fills the far wall, the room completely empty and waiting, the quiet held stillness of the half hour before a difficult meeting, every plane from the near chair backs to the far mountains in crisp deep focus.

The room belongs to the administrative office of a copper mining company in the Armenian highlands in 2026, a sober recently renovated interior: pale warm-grey painted walls, the long left wall clad in honey-pink local volcanic tuff stone blocks with fine pores and soft chisel texture, a long walnut-veneer conference table with a satin finish showing faint fingerprints and a few fine scratches near the near end, ten grey mesh office chairs set along both sides with clear gaps between them, two chairs on the right pulled slightly back and turned at different angles as if people had just stood up, the near-left chair pushed squarely in. A flat screen on the right wall is switched off and shows a dim grey reflection of the window. On a low credenza against the stone wall sit three white safety helmets with scuffed shells and a folded high-visibility vest. On the table: a shallow wooden tray of split drill-core samples in grey rock with veins of brassy yellow and patches of green and blue copper staining, a rolled survey plan held open at one corner by a stone sample, a glass water carafe with a few tumblers, a closed laptop, a pen lying across a notepad with handwriting that is too small to read, and at the near right place a small white coffee cup with dark grounds dried at the bottom of the cup and on its saucer. Faint dust settles on the stone ledge by the window, and a desk plant with slightly drooping leaves stands in the far corner. All papers, screens and signage are faded and unreadable at this distance.

Through the window, in the middle distance, a vast open-pit copper mine fills the view: wide stepped benches cut down into the mountainside in bands of rust-ochre, ash grey, pale bleached yellow and muted grey-green oxidized rock, switchback haul roads zigzagging down the terraces, a few large dump trucks as small yellow shapes on the lower benches, a faint plume of dust hanging over one working face, waste-rock terraces spreading beyond. Behind the pit rise bare high treeless mountain ridges in brown and slate tones with a light dusting of early snow on the highest crests, the far ridges fading into soft grey atmospheric haze under a low even overcast sky. The pit's colors sit muted and true, a modest part of the frame, read through clean window glass with a faint reflection of the room.

The only light is flat overcast daylight from the window: a soft even cool-neutral wash that travels down the table, catches the satin veneer in a long dull reflection of the window, and falls off gently toward the camera end, the ceiling light panels switched off. The overcast sky is the brightest value in the frame and keeps its subtle cloud structure without clipping. The darkest value is the shadow under the table and between the chair legs, deep but with detail. Soft contact shadows sit under the chairs, under the carafe, under the core tray and along the base of the stone wall. The exposure balances the interior and the exterior view together, with no artificial light anywhere.

Captured with a natural spherical 28mm-equivalent lens at a stopped-down aperture, straight vertical lines, the room and the distant mine both resolving sharply, a fine-grain daylight color-negative film rendition with gentle highlight roll-off, a restrained natural grade with muted earth tones, true neutral greys and a faintly cool overcast cast, true color and true scale, in a quiet observational documentary-drama register. A real photographic frame captured on a real camera in a real highland office: real tuff stone, real walnut veneer, real mesh fabric, real rock and real haze. No CGI, no rendered look, no digital cleanliness, no plastic surfaces, no AI smoothness, no glossy highlights, no glow, no teal-and-orange grade, no people.
```

**Settings:** Banana Pro, 16:9, 2K, 2–4 variations. If the window view comes out too bright or too faint, keep the interior as it is and add a separate exterior plate of the pit later, using the same overcast light.

**Checks:** there are no people, names, brands or readable text, and no references were used. The only light source is the window, and its direction holds across the frame. The brightest and darkest values are named, and the contact shadows are kept. Focus runs deep throughout, so nothing in the prompt asks for blurred backgrounds.
